In order to fill a fixed-term position in full-time (39.83 hours/week = 100%;) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for 1

Environmental research with liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry with a focus on Soil Science

The Soil Science and Soil Resources Group (Prof. Ines Mulder) investigates biogeochemical processes in soils and develops analytical methods to characterize anthropogenic substances in soils and urban ecosystems.

The focus of this position is on the application and further development of high-resolution mass spectrometric methods in combination with liquid chromatography to detect organic micro-pollutants in complex soil and environmental samples. The research concentrates on disinfectants, pharmaceutical residues, and other organic trace substances, whose entry into (peri-)urban soils may alter ecosystem functioning.

Scope: full-time
Duration: fixed-term, 3 years
Start: at the earliest possible date
Apply by:  2026-08-31

Your tasks:

- Project management for the quantification of disinfectants and antibiotics in environmental samples using UPLC-MS/MS and UPLC-HRMS, including laboratory and data analysis work
- Establishment of an analytical platform for organic trace substance analysis in cooperation with the Hydrogeochemistry Group, including administration, data, and quality assurance
- Further development of existing analytical methods, including non-target analysis
- Method development for the analysis of novel compounds from environmental samples
- Conducting field and laboratory work for data collection
- Preparation and publication of project results in scientific journals
- Opportunity to apply for and develop your own projects
- Teaching up to 4 hours per week per semester for geography students and supporting students during data collection, evaluation, and analysis for theses

Your profile:

- Master’s degree in environmental sciences, geography, earth sciences, environmental analytics, or a similar discipline
- Completed doctoratewith a relevant focus is desirable
- Enthusiasm for soil science topics
- Knowledge in analytical chemistry and statistical methods is required
- Strong interest in a scientific career
- Interest in publishing in German and English
- Experience in university teaching is an advantage
- Excellent knowledge of the German language (for teaching) or willingness to learn German
- Excellent English language skills (written and spoken)
- Willingness to perform independent laboratory and field work
- Willingness to travel and undertake multi-day to multi-week international stays for sampling campaigns

jobs.description:
The Faculty of Process and Systems Engineering, Chair of Mechanical Process Engineering seeks to fill the following vacancy:

Junior Group Leader (m/f/d) in Computational Multiphase Flow

Salary scale:
13 TV-L

Date commencing:
As soon as possible

Fixed term:
3 years*

Contract status:
100 %

At the Chair of Mechanical Process Engineering (www.mvt.ovgu.de), we are a group of enthusiastic researchers with extensive research activities in the numerical modelling of multiphase flows. Our work addresses the fundamental physical mechanisms governing dispersed and interfacial multiphase flows, as well as their application to engineering systems. Current research topics include particle-laden and droplet-laden turbulent flows, particle–turbulence and droplet–turbulence interactions, the dynamics of non-spherical particles, interfacial flows, and compressible and incompressible multiphase-flow applications. Approximately eight PhD researchers and three postdoctoral researchers currently work in this area at the Chair.

The objective of the advertised position is to attract a junior group leader who will take a leading role in our computational multiphase-flow research. The successful candidate will contribute to and help coordinate ongoing research projects, while also establishing their own research direction within the Chair. The position offers excellent opportunities to develop an independent academic profile and to pursue a Habilitation. It therefore combines scientific leadership in existing activities with the opportunity to initiate new research topics and contribute to the further development of our numerical methods and simulation tools.

Our in-house simulation framework includes state-of-the-art methods for immersed boundaries, Lagrangian particle and droplet tracking, non-spherical particle dynamics, particle and droplet interactions, gas–liquid interfaces, large-eddy simulation, and fully coupled solvers for compressible and incompressible flows. You will also have the opportunity to establish your own teaching portfolio in areas such as numerical methods, multiphase flows, or particle technology.

*The position is full time for a period of 3 years with the opportunity to extend by a further 3 years.

Job description:

- Develop, implement, and analyse analytical and numerical models for multiphase flows
- Establish an independent research profile in computational multiphase-flow modelling
- Lead and coordinate the further development of our in-house simulation tools in C and MPI
- Develop research ideas and prepare proposals for externally funded research projects
- Supervise PhD researchers, postdoctoral researchers, and students working in computational multiphase flows
- Contribute to teaching in multiphase flows, numerical methods, particle technology, or related subjects
- Contribute to the scientific development and coordination of the computational multiphase-flow group
- Opportunity for further scientific qualification, including the possibility to pursue a Habilitation

Requirements profile:

- A Master’s degree or equivalent and a PhD in mechanical engineering, process engineering, aerospace engineering, applied mathematics, physics, or a related discipline
- A strong background in the physical and numerical modelling of fluid-mechanical or multiphase-flow problems
- Demonstrated research experience in computational multiphase flows, such as particle-laden, droplet-laden, or interfacial flows
- Strong scientific-programming skills in C, C++, or Fortran, including experience with MPI and high-performance computing
- Experience in developing numerical methods or simulation software; expertise in techniques such as immersed-boundary methods, Lagrangian tracking, interface-capturing methods, or particle-interaction models is desirable
- A strong publication record commensurate with your career stage, together with the ability to develop independent research ideas and contribute to research proposals
- Excellent written and spoken English, as well as a good command of German or a commitment to acquiring sufficient German proficiency for teaching and administrative duties within two years

For further information about the position, please contact Prof. Berend van Wachem by email, berend.vanwachem(at)ovgu.de

You will benefit from our structures and offerings in the fields of sustainability, diversity, family support and staff development. Our location in the center of a thriving, lively and family-friendly state capital guarantees a high quality of life and a wide range of leisure activities. Fairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.

 Fairtrade International is an independent non-profit organisation representing more than two million small-scale farmers and workers worldwide. Beyond certification, Fairtrade International and its member organisations (three producer networks and 19 national Fairtrade organisations) partner with producers and businesses, engage consumers, and advocate for a fair and sustainable future.

Unit’s description and purpose:

The Global Advocacy unit leads Fairtrade International's policy and citizen engagement efforts, supporting the "Inspire a collective commitment to fair and sustainable trade" pillar of the 2026–2028 Global Strategy. It amplifies the voices of farmers and workers, informs and influences policy, and builds partnerships that strengthen representation and equity in sustainable supply chains — positioning Fairtrade as a leading, coherent voice in sustainable trade at EU, global, and local levels.

Role purpose:

The Global Advocacy Lead guides Fairtrade International's advocacy work and directly manages the Global Advocacy team, supporting the wider Fairtrade system's efforts to multiply impact through proven producer-driven solutions that deliver policy and practice change for smallholder farmers and workers globally.

Following a recent review of Fairtrade's advocacy work, the post holder works closely with the Fairtrade Advocacy Community of Practice — the three producer networks, 19 national organisations, and the Fair Trade Advocacy Office (FTAO) — to reshape advocacy output and build on existing successes. Given Fairtrade's lean global centre and inter-dependent structure, the role's focus is on directly managing the Global Advocacy team while providing leadership, coherence, and a unified advocacy output.

Best Practice and Skill Development — approx. 10%

Team Management and Relationships — approx. 20%
